cell_biology.objective: Describe the structure and function of the cell membrane, nucleus, mitochondria, and endoplasmic reticulum.

homeostasis.objective: Define homeostasis; explain negative and positive feedback mechanisms with physiological examples.

nervous_system.objective: Describe neuron structure, resting potential, action potential generation, and synaptic transmission.

cardiovascular_system.objective: Explain the cardiac cycle, heart rate regulation, blood pressure determinants, and the role of the autonomic nervous system.

respiratory_system.objective: Describe the mechanics of breathing, lung volumes, gas exchange at the alveolus, and the oxyhemoglobin dissociation curve.

ecg_basics.objective: Identify the P, QRS, and T waves on an ECG trace and relate them to the phases of the cardiac cycle.

muscular_system.objective: Explain the sliding filament model of muscle contraction, the role of calcium and ATP, and motor unit recruitment.

endocrine_system.objective: Describe hormone classification, receptor binding, and feedback control with examples from the hypothalamic-pituitary axis.

renal_system.objective: Explain glomerular filtration, tubular reabsorption and secretion, and how the kidney regulates fluid and electrolyte balance.

biosignal_origins.objective: Explain the physiological origins of ECG, EMG, and EEG biosignals and relate waveform features to underlying physiology.

notes: 10-topic Physiology Basics domain for the curric-agents pilot study.
